record_type_quote: This replication attempts to test the main claim from LeBoeuf & Simmons (2010) that products predominantly associated with utilitarian attitudes at the product category level support less utilitarian and more symbolic attitudes at the brand level, while products predominantly associated with symbolic attitudes at the product category level support less symbolic and more utilitarian attitudes at the brand level (H1).

targets.authors: LeBoeuf, R. A., & Simmons, J. P.
targets.title: Branding alters attitude functions and reduces the advantage of function-matching persuasive appeals.
targets.evidence_quote: This replication attempts to test the main claim from LeBoeuf & Simmons (2010) that products predominantly associated with utilitarian attitudes at the product category level support less utilitarian and more symbolic attitudes at the brand level, while products predominantly associated with symbolic attitudes at the product category level support less symbolic and more utilitarian attitudes at the brand level (H1).
targets.outcome_quote: There was a significant interaction of Level x Product Type on the benefit rating - symbolism rating difference scores (F(1, 555) = 10.89, p = 0.001, two-tailed, partial eta squared = 0.02; see the figure below), such that products that support symbolic attitudes are associated more utilitarian attitudes when branded, while products that support utilitarian attitudes are associated more with symbolic attitudes when branded.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Central interaction significant in original direction, satisfying stated replication criterion; post-hoc pattern explicitly consistent with original.
